terms.sub: Cerebral Cortex Layers, Functional Areas, and Hemispheric Lateralization
clues: It results from a lesion of the right (non-dominant) posterior parietal cortex
Patients eat food only from the right half of their plate or draw numbers only on the right side of a clock
They fail to attend to the left half of space and their own left limbs despite intact primary vision
Also called central post-stroke thalamic pain syndrome, it follows an infarct in the VPL and VPM nuclei
Weeks to months after initial numbness, patients develop agonizing contralateral burning pain
Light touch or minor temperature changes trigger severe dysesthetic allodynia
This 8 to 13 Hz EEG waveform is maximal over the parieto-occipital cortex
It appears in a relaxed, awake person with their eyes closed
Opening the eyes or performing mental arithmetic immediately abolishes it in a phenomenon called alpha block

terms.sub: Sleep Architecture: NREM Stages, REM Sleep, and Circadian Rhythm
clues: Also called paradoxical sleep, its EEG shows low-voltage desynchronized beta and sawtooth waves
It features vivid narrative dreaming, autonomic variability, and active glycinergic skeletal muscle atonia
Its episodes recur every ~90 minutes and lengthen during the final third of the night

terms.sub: Sleep Architecture: NREM Stages, REM Sleep, and Circadian Rhythm
clues: Type 1 cases result from autoimmune loss of orexin (hypocretin) neurons in the lateral hypothalamus
Polysomnography demonstrates characteristic sleep-onset REM periods (SOREMPs)
Patients suffer irresistible daytime sleep attacks, laughter-triggered cataplexy, sleep paralysis, and hypnagogic hallucinations

terms.sub: Language Pathways and Aphasias (Broca, Wernicke, Conduction, Global)
clues: It is caused by infarction of the left inferior frontal gyrus (Brodmann areas 44 and 45) via the superior MCA division
Patients produce non-fluent, effortful, telegraphic speech while retaining intact comprehension
Repetition is impaired and patients are acutely aware and frustrated by their speech deficit

terms.sub: Language Pathways and Aphasias (Broca, Wernicke, Conduction, Global)
clues: It results from damage to the left posterior superior temporal gyrus (Brodmann area 22)
Patients speak in fluent, effortless, grammatical-sounding 'word salad' filled with paraphasias
Both auditory/reading comprehension and repetition are severely impaired, and patients lack insight

terms.sub: Language Pathways and Aphasias (Broca, Wernicke, Conduction, Global)
clues: It is caused by a lesion of the left arcuate fasciculus connecting temporal and frontal language areas
Both spontaneous speech fluency and auditory comprehension remain intact
Its hallmark deficit is a severe inability to repeat spoken phrases, accompanied by phonemic self-correction

terms.sub: Language Pathways and Aphasias (Broca, Wernicke, Conduction, Global)
clues: Also called pure word blindness, it follows a left Posterior Cerebral Artery occlusion
The stroke destroys both the left visual cortex and the splenium of the corpus callosum
The patient can write a coherent sentence normally yet cannot read what they just wrote

terms.sub: Limbic System, Papez Circuit, and Amygdala
clues: It results from bilateral destruction of the amygdalae, classically following herpes simplex encephalitis
Patients exhibit profound placidity and loss of fear or anger
Other hallmark features include hyperorality, hypersexuality, and visual agnosia

terms.sub: CSF Production, Circulation, Blood-Brain Barrier, and Hydrocephalus
clues: It causes ventriculomegaly in older adults with normal opening pressure on lumbar puncture
Its classic clinical triad ('wet, wobbly, and wacky') comprises urinary incontinence, magnetic gait apraxia, and dementia
Symptoms often improve transiently after a large-volume CSF tap and permanently after shunting

terms.sub: CSF Production, Circulation, Blood-Brain Barrier, and Hydrocephalus
clues: It is a life-threatening physiological sign of critically elevated intracranial pressure
Brainstem ischemia triggers sympathetic vasoconstriction followed by baroreceptor-mediated vagal slowing
It consists of hypertension with widened pulse pressure, bradycardia, and irregular respirations
